summary: Fountain Valley sits on a dead-flat coastal plain just four miles from the Pacific, yet it has no coastline of its own — a geographic quirk that gives it mild, marine-layer-moderated weather (average highs around 73°F year-round, with 9.2 hours of daily sunshine) without the premium that beachfront cities command. The city's 9.1 square miles are compact and almost entirely built out, packed at over 6,200 people per square mile, which means the street grid reads continuous residential rather than sprawling — Mile Square Regional Park, a 640-acre rectangle of sports fields, lakes, and walking paths right in the center, functions as the de facto backyard for a huge swath of the city. Hyundai's U.S. headquarters and MemorialCare's Orange Coast Medical Center anchor a legitimate local employment base, so this isn't purely a bedroom community, though the 405 freeway bisects the city and shapes the commute reality for many. The affordability math is stark: a median home price just above $1 million against a median household income of roughly $112,000 yields a price-to-income ratio over 9:1, while median rent at $2,507 consumes about 27% of that same gross income — manageable for renters, punishing for buyers without substantial equity. Fountain Valley is essentially a mid-density Orange County grid town where the park is bigger than the personality.
